title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not original Grothendieck mathematics. It is page 2 of a typescript of P. Deligne's 'Courbes elliptiques : formulaire (d'après J. Tate)', published in Modular Functions of One Variable IV, LNM 476, 1975. The wording and the numbering (1.1), (1.2), (1.3) match the published Formulaire. The only additions are blue pen marks: two vertical strokes and two marginal 'réf' (reference wanted). They are probably by Grothendieck or a reader of his copy.

The mathematics: p: E → S is a generalized elliptic curve (a cubic curve over S) with unit section e, and ω = e^*Ω^1. The page builds the Weierstrass equation over an arbitrary base.
(i) R^1 p_* O(ne) = 0 for n > 0, checked fibre by fibre. With Riemann–Roch and cohomology and base change, p_*O(ne) is locally free of rank n and its formation commutes with base change.
(ii) Restricting O((n+1)e) to the section gives e^*O(e)^{⊗(n+1)}. Since e^*O(e) is the normal bundle ω^{-1}, the residue sequence gives 0 → p_*O(ne) → p_*O((n+1)e) → ω^{⊗-(n+1)} → 0.
(iii) O_S ≅ p_*O_E ≅ p_*O(e): there are no functions with a single simple pole, using SGA 1 X 1.2.
(iv) Hence p_*O(ne) has a filtration with graded pieces ω^{⊗-i}, for 0 ≤ i ≤ n and i ≠ 1. This is formula (1.1).
(v) p is a relative complete intersection, so Rp^!O_S has a single nonzero cohomology sheaf. That sheaf is invertible: the sheaf of regular (dualizing) differentials Ω^reg_{E/S}, equal to Ω^1_{E/S} where p is smooth.
(vi) Grothendieck duality gives R^1 p_* Ω^reg ≅ O_S. So p_*Ω^reg is locally free and commutes with base change. On the next page it is identified with ω, which defines the invariant differentials.

Purpose: choose a basis (x, y, 1) of p_*O(3e) adapted to the filtration. This yields the Weierstrass equation y^2 + a1 xy + a3 y = x^3 + ... and the coordinate-change formulas (1.2). These underlie Tate's formulaire for c4, c6, Δ and j, and the modular-forms computations on the previous page.
errors: In the typescript the nonzero cohomology of Rp^!O_S is written as degree 1 ('R^1 p^! O_S'). For a relative curve, p^!O_S = Ω^reg[1], so with the standard convention the nonzero sheaf sits in degree -1. This is a convention or typo issue only; it affects nothing downstream.
The filtration statement silently uses that p_*O(e) = p_*O_E. This is why the index i = 1 is missing from (1.1); the text states it correctly via (iii).

The vertical-stroke insertion marks and the two 'réf' annotations indicate that a reader wanted references for the complete-intersection/duality claims and for the base-change claim; no references are supplied.

ideas.what: Filtration of p_*O(ne) on a generalized elliptic curve, with graded pieces ω^{-i} for i ≠ 1
ideas.modern_name: Weierstrass equations over an arbitrary base (Riemann–Roch filtration)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a copy of Deligne's published 'Formulaire' (LNM 476), with only marginal 'réf' marks added. It contains no original Grothendieck mathematics. Its archival interest is only that Grothendieck kept and read this text while working on Hasse invariants and Gauss–Manin connections (previous page).
transcription_corrections: The '{+/+}' tokens are blue vertical insertion strokes in the margin of the text, each paired with a blue marginal 'réf'. The first is after 'D^+(E)'; the second is before 'localement libre'.
'La dualité montre que R^1 p_* Ω^reg_{E/S} est isomorphe à O': here O means O_S.
The degree in 'R^1 p^! O_S' is as typed. Mathematically it should be degree -1 under standard conventions.
